answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with a burn-per-action toll: every trade or vote requires destroying a small amount of the network token. Think of it like a timber orchard — a fable says a forester who plants one tree pays once, but someone planting ten thousand saplings must pay for every seedling. Honest agents pay the toll once per real action, a trivial cost; an attacker running thousands of fake identities must burn the toll for each one, so the price of a fake army rises linearly with its size until forgery costs more than any gain.
